name: GIQ
description: Monocular 3D reconstruction methods and vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate impressive results on standard benchmarks, yet their true understanding of geometric properties remains unclear. We introduce GIQ , a comprehensive benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the geometric reasoning capabilities of vision and vision-language foundation models. GIQ comprises synthetic and real-world images of 224 diverse polyhedra - including Platonic, Archimedean, Johnson, and Catalan solids, as well as stellations and compound shapes - covering varying levels of complexity and symmetry. Through systematic experiments involving monocular 3D reconstruction, 3D symmetry detection, mental rotation tests, and zero-shot shape classification tasks, we reveal significant shortcomings in current models. State-of-the-art reconstruction algorithms trained on extensive 3D datasets struggle to reconstruct even basic geometric forms accurately. While foundation models effectively detect specific 3D symmetry elements via linear probing, they falter significantly in tasks requiring detailed geometric differentiation, such as mental rotation. Moreover, advanced vision-language assistants exhibit remarkably low accuracy on complex polyhedra, systematically misinterpreting basic properties like face geometry, convexity, and compound structures. GIQ is publicly available, providing a structured platform to highlight and address critical gaps in geometric intelligence, facilitating future progress in robust, geometry-aware representation learning.
evaluation_method: task-specific metrics (classification: accuracy; symmetry/rotation: accuracy or match rate; reconstruction: Chamfer distance / reconstruction error)
general_score_metric: accuracy (for classification/symmetry tasks) and Chamfer distance / reconstruction error (for 3D reconstruction)
reputation: New benchmark (arXiv:2506.08194) designed to expose geometric reasoning gaps in vision and VLMs; likely to attract attention from researchers in geometry-aware vision.
notes: Contains both synthetic and real images of 224 polyhedra — useful for focused geometric evaluation but limited in class count relative to large-scale vision datasets. Tasks are diverse so performance is metric-dependent; not primarily an LLM benchmark.
